title: Exponential Moving Average

statement.md: An exponential moving average (EMA) with span $s$ weighs recent prices more than old ones. It uses the smoothing factor $\alpha = 2 / (s + 1)$ and is **seeded with the first price**:

Print $e_i$ for every day, each with exactly 4 decimal places. Compute with ordinary double precision numbers in the order written above; the tests keep every printed value away from a rounding tie, so any sensible double implementation agrees.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $s$. Second line: $n$ prices, each a positive number with at most two decimal digits.
constraints: No printed value lies within $10^{-8}$ of a rounding tie at the fourth decimal
hints: Keep one running value. Initialise it with the first price, then update it once per remaining price.
With span 1, alpha is 1, so the EMA equals the price series.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "The recurrence needs only the previous value, so the series costs $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ extra memory. A span of $s$ corresponds to $\\alpha = 2/(s+1)$, so a span of 9 gives $\\alpha = 0.2$."}, {"type": "p", "md": "Seeding with the first price (not with 0 or with an average of the first $s$ prices) is part of the specification. Seeding with 0 pulls the early values far below the prices."}]

solutions.python:
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, span = int(tok[0]), int(tok[1])
    alpha = 2.0 / (span + 1)
    ema = float(tok[2])
    out = [f"{ema:.4f}"]
    for s in tok[3:2 + n]:
        ema = alpha * float(s) + (1 - alpha) * ema
        out.append(f"{ema:.4f}")
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()
